doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

title: Ernest O'Cos, barrelhouse pianist
summary: Burns describes O'Cos, who worked in France, played barrelhouse, and died decades earlier.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Oh, he was a Barrelhouse player?
Yeah, yeah. Yeah, yeah. He was a Barrelhouse player. O'Cos. Yeah.
Yeah, Ernest O'Cos. Yeah, he been dead. 35, 40 years. Oh, 40 years at least.
He was a New Orleans man. Yeah, sure. What else do you know about him? I never heard his name before.
Well, he went to France. He was a, he worked, oh, way back there, unloading ships there in France. Him and his dad both. He went with his dad. And he used to play this ballhouse blues and piano.

Oh, he was around me. He was a little older than me. He wasn't much. Oh, yeah. He may have been about two or three years or so, older than me. Oh, I see. Yeah. He was old like Swan, Sonny Swan and Jim Fisher.
